open_obligations: Note that the protocol is not recursive and debaters are not trained to equilibrium.
Check whether the prior-dependent gains count as a systematic judge error of the kind Buhl et al. worry about.
Note other questions in Buhl et al.'s list (equilibrium, stability, obfuscation) are not addressed.
in.other_title: AI debate helps biased human judges assess controversial COVID-19 and climate claims
in.rationale: Buhl et al. note most debate experiments use QuALITY with simple low-depth protocols and ask whether debate measurably improves performance and what systematic errors humans make. Rahman et al. report debate improves human accuracy and calibration over consultancy on COVID-19 and climate claims, with smaller gains for skeptical-prior judges; protocols are three-round prompted GPT-4o debates, not trained recursive debate.
in.scope: proposed ADDRESSES: whether debate measurably improves human judgement outside QuALITY, for contested scientific claims

text: The authors say there is only limited data on debate's practical effectiveness, with most experiments using the QuALITY dataset and simple low-depth protocols. They list as key questions whether debate measurably improves performance, whether training reliably reaches equilibrium, whether stability is a real problem, whether obfuscated arguments emerge as predicted, how good humans are and what systematic errors they make, and deployment questions such as what counts as an action and whether domain questions are hard to answer with deductive arguments.
title: Open empirical questions: does debate help, reach equilibrium, show obfuscation?
